images.name: The Ebb-Tide Landing
images.description: A slick pier meets the steps at the water's edge; the salt-worn outlines of ruins fade into pale grey fog.
images.background: Mistport's Undertow goes under at flood tide, and explorers may go in only for a short while after the ebb. The ruins it uncovers may be laid out differently every time, so knowing the tide and when to get out is safer than trusting an old map.
images.storyContext: A mood piece showing one way down at the ebb; it does not fix the layout of the next ebb. It helps the player grasp how little can be seen in the fog, how the tide line shifts, and why a way back matters.
images.location: A waterside passage between Mid-Harbor and the Undertow
visualNotes: Ropes, shells and wet planks are sharp up close; the distance is lost entirely in fog.
The steps lead to nearby broken walls; the picture does not show the whole city.
The hanging lamp has no open flame, in keeping with quiet, low-light exploration.

images.name: Appraisal by Lamplight
images.description: A mood piece: Su Yao examines an ordinary relic awaiting appraisal, without revealing what it does or anything about the central mystery.
images.background: Su Yao is a full Tide-Reader and assistant to Guildmaster Qi. Relics can have unpredictable effects, and the Guild's appraisal procedure makes finds, records and evidence a central part of any investigation in Mistport.
images.storyContext: The still shows routine appraisal work. The fragment on the cloth has no assigned role in the plot; do not take it as part of any key, or as proven safe.
visualNotes: Su Yao's face, pinned-up hair, high-collared coat and round appraisal mirror match her original portrait.
Cold tide-stone light falls on the workbench; there is no open flame and no magic beam.
Records, measuring tools and an unnamed fragment carry the investigation theme.

images.name: Lin Yuanzhou
images.description: A young apprentice holds a cold-light fog-lamp; his dark collar blends into the wet harbor, and a faint mark shows at his wrist.
images.background: Lin Yuanzhou has just passed his first Tide-Reader Guild exam; he is careful, and full of curiosity. For a player who chooses the apprentice background, he is an important peer on joining the Guild.
images.storyContext: Use it to introduce him when the player first meets the Guild or prepares an expedition. The lamp shows the Undertow's need for low light and quiet; the portrait gives away none of the secrets he has not told.
visualNotes: The lamp in his hand gives cold light; the warm harbor lights in the distance do not mean he carries a torch.

images.name: Su Yao
images.description: Su Yao wears a dark Guild uniform with fine gold trim and holds a round appraisal mirror; her look is focused and restrained.
images.background: Su Yao is a full Tide-Reader and Old Qi's assistant. Rigorous in her work, she is the player's bridge to the Guild's leadership; if the player chose the apprentice background, she was also the examiner at the entrance exam.
images.storyContext: After Qi disappears, she comes looking for the player on the Main Pier with half a letter. Use the portrait to introduce her profession and why she seeks you out at the start; any specific appraisal result in the mirror must still come from the story.
visualNotes: The round mirror is a tool of her trade; the image gives no reading that could establish what a relic does.

images.name: Iron Meg
images.description: Iron Meg's messy short hair, scarred jaw, dark leathers and folded arms make a hard silhouette; her left forearm gives off a translucent grey mist.
images.background: Iron Meg, in her thirties, is second-in-command of the Salt Fangs. A relic accident left her left arm fog-rotted below the elbow. Cold, hard and true to her word, she forbids her people to sell dangerous unappraised relics to civilians who don't know what they're buying.
images.storyContext: Use it to introduce the Undertow's underworld order and the price of fog-rot. Her trust in the player, the terms of any deal and any later cooperation have to be built in the story.
visualNotes: The fog-rot is on her own left arm — the forearm crossing her waist on the right side of the picture. The grey mist should not be read as ice or lightning.

images.name: Chen Yuanshan
images.description: A grey-haired elder in a dark, embroidered robe holds up a dark, angular fragment. He smiles, but his gaze is appraising.
images.background: Chen Yuanshan, past sixty, chairs the Mistport Council and is pushing the Seal Tide Decree to restrict civilian access to the Undertow. The Council controls the Upper City and the legal relic trade, so his orders decide directly who may go on an expedition.
images.storyContext: Good for introducing the Council's power, permits, and the pressure of the lockdown. The image does not establish where the fragment in his hand came from, what it does, or what he is searching for.
visualNotes: The fragment is described only as an angular object; its shape does not give it a quest number or make it part of a key.

images.name: Old Qi
images.description: White-haired and white-bearded, Old Qi holds a thick book. His face is gentle, and faint grey, translucent traces hang around his hands.
images.background: Old Qi is Guildmaster of the Tide-Reader Guild and cares more about research than politics. As the game opens, he has left a letter, gone into the Undertow and disappeared — during the flood tide, when it should have been impossible to get in.
images.storyContext: Good for his character file, the clues to his disappearance and background on the Guild. The portrait is a character reference: it does not mean the player has found him, and it does not explain how he got into ruins under the flood.
visualNotes: The book and the patches of fog-rot follow his established look; the image reveals neither what is in the book nor what caused the symptoms.

images.name: Frost
images.description: A girl with long, pale hair, in a robe that covers her completely, tilts her head and raises one hand to her ear; her fingertips fade into a faint mist.
images.background: Frost is a young Mist-Speaker of the Congregation of the Mist, about fifteen or sixteen. She claims to hear the fog whispering and has accurately predicted the timing of ebbs and the location of ruins, but where her prophecies come from remains a mystery.
images.storyContext: Use it to introduce the Congregation and the open question of the fog's whispers. The tilted head shows someone listening; it neither proves the fog has a will nor counts as an act of magic.
visualNotes: Only the faint mist and the listening pose are recorded; her looks imply no power rank and no family tie.

images.name: Grey Falcon
images.description: A short-haired man in a dark coat with an insignia holds a tightly shuttered metal fog-lamp that lets out only a thin slit of cold light.
images.background: Grey Falcon is captain of Chen Yuanshan's private expedition and enforces the Seal Tide Decree. A man of few words and great efficiency, he handles cordons, searches and pursuit.
images.storyContext: Use it to show how Council orders press on the harbor and the entrances to the ruins. At the start, his hunt crosses the trail of Qi's disappearance; the portrait does not decide whether he keeps obeying later.
visualNotes: The metal lamp is recognizable by its shutters and faint cold light; never describe it as a flaming torch.

images.name: The Harbor in Perpetual Mist
images.description: Wet stone walkways and ruins bared by the ebb lead to the harbor in the foreground; cranes, boats and towers built up the cliff fade tier by tier into grey fog, lit here and there by warm lamps.
images.background: Mistport climbs the cliff in three tiers: the Upper City, Mid-Harbor and the Undertow. The relic trade keeps the city alive; the ebb bares the ruins and the flood drowns the lowest tier, and after every Riftide the layout of the ruins changes.
images.storyContext: A promotional overview of the harbor city that uses stacked buildings to show a vertical city. Actual exploration still keeps to fog visibility of no more than fifty paces; the cover is not a ruin map to be reused.
visualNotes: The city's warm lamps are not the cold tide-stone lamps used to explore the Undertow; the broken arch in the picture is not identified as the Bone Arch from any particular deep withdrawal.
